sentences.text: You?
Yeah, I'm good, thanks.
This meeting is being recorded.
Switching everything on.
Yeah.
Good.
Whereabouts you both?
London, sort of.
Mostly between London and New York, but I'm at home at the moment, so just started working for Kevor who are a remote first business which will take a little getting used to, I think.
Well, we've been remote for a long time, so.
So yeah, it does get some taking used to.
Where, where were you before?
I was at a Dutch listed company called Azerian, so I was sort of moving between our office in New York and.
And in Waterloo.
Right, okay, cool.
Well, I'm in Somerset today, but yeah, sometimes London as well, sometimes New York.
Very nice.
So I notice you filled in a form, so be interested to understand what it is that you're looking to do and obviously if we can help you, I'll be happy to do that as well.
Just a bit of background about us.
I think it came through the agency's website, but we are capital A group, so under that umbrella there is capital A and agencies.
Co agencies is our platform for agency owners to buy and sell.

And also we work on the buy and sell side as capital A, helping mostly agency owners that are scaling up through inorganic growth, but sometimes private equity, but certainly private equity backed holding companies, helping them to target businesses to acquire.
But we help the entire journey from start to finish.
So quite experienced in the whole agency space and we're only focused on marketing services, so that's our specialty really.
So yeah, it'd be great to hear a little bit more about what it is that you're doing and.
Yeah, let's see if we can help you.
Yeah, sure.
Well, it seems to be worth a conversation and I guess we'll flush out fairly quickly whether that's.
That's kind of right or not.
So very, very brief potted background.
I used to run a business called Inskin Media, which is a rich media vendor based in the uk, mostly orientated towards Europe and Asia rather than the States.
Sold that to Aerion in 21.
Joined their M A team for a year.

Kick the tires on a bunch, bunch of businesses we ended up buying, eight of which I was on the deal team for two out of the back of that we ended up with, let's say, people and relationships and contracts and revenue and so on in the US which is how I came to take on the US business.
So integrated those three businesses and then sort of ran it for, you know, for the last three years essentially.

And then about halfway through that stint took over the UK and I've Just joined Kevl and the reason that that sort of stuff is relevant is that at Azerian we use inorganic growth acquisition as a pretty material commercial strategy.
And my let's say intention alignment with sort of the CAVAL board is that we will use the same lever as one of a number of things that we'll want to do.
So Kevl's acquired I think two businesses in its history but we're definitely on the lookout for more.
And I'll circle back to what that sort of looks like in just a second.
Just in terms of the business itself, it's really a business that provides the technology to retailers to become their own retail media network.
That's the sort of, the very, very short version.
Over the last three or four years they've built a client base with a couple hundred clients ranging from the likes of PayPal to Chewy to Home Depot etc.
And we're now trying to build a media business kind of on the top of that so that we can bring those clients demand just as much as they can generate their own demand, if you see what I mean.

And so where that sort of takes us to is, you know, I'm starting to look for let's say sales houses in particular, but doesn't have to be who are somewhat or very what in the retail media space who could be a interesting target by, by which I mean nothing huge, probably sub 20 million of revenue, UK, US orientated.
But apart from that, apart from that I was all quite open minded about what that might sort of look like, if you see what I mean.
The key is that we do want to accelerate building this business and aqua hiring rather than sort of hiring one person at a time would seem to be a pretty good way to go about that.
So that's the context.
Okay, cool.
So we actually, well we can actually work in two ways.
One is that we are obviously listing businesses for sale.
So anything in shopper media we can certainly put in front of you.
And we do have a client currently which is a UK based shopper media SaaS platform.
7 million in revenue.
$7 million.
I don't know if you've seen that listed on agencies, maybe that was why you came through there.
But certainly I can share that with you.
I'll give you the link now so you've got it, but I'll follow up.
Thank you afterwards.
But that's in the chat as well if you want to peruse in the meantime and obviously if you're part of a bigger company, I guess it really depends what you're looking to do and how quick.
But we work on the buy side as well.
So we work with clients like yourselves, where we're just teeing up those deals for you, basically.

So we go out and build a list of potential targets and then we do all of the legwork, do the preliminary calls and kind of bring them to the table and then set up the calls with you and help land it, basically.
What does the sort of the commercial model for that look like?
So we work on a retained basis.
We take one and a half percent on the deals as well when they close.
So currently charge around $5,000 a month.
Yeah.
Let's just jot this down as we go.
It's a lot less than it used to be about two months ago in pounds.
So.
So, yeah, we work on a retained basis.
Usually we have a minimum requirement of three months, but that's because it takes us about three or four weeks get up and running.
So.

But, but just to be realistic, about the first two or three weeks is really building the, the pipeline and building the list of targets and then outreaching to them and then, you know, teeing them all up.
So by week 4 ish of the first month, we're starting to book stuff into your calendar.
Got it.
Okay.
Yeah.
I mean, I've, I've.
I mean, I've worked with, with people a bit like that in the past.
I mean, I've got no idea what, what, how Kev want to sort of play this, if you see what I mean.
I say it's only, it's only day two is the reality.
But, you know, we'll find out fairly quickly.

I mean, we've said, we've certainly kind of agreed that this is, this is, this is one of the tools that we need to, to use, but I don't really know how they've sourced deals in the past in, in any great sort of detail, so.
Okay.
I mean, I guess that's sort of the long and the short of it really, isn't it, you know, when it comes to it.
So let me take a look at what you just sent over.
Yeah.
So check out that.
As Project McLaren, these guys are in the, the process now.
We have three other buyers at the table.
Okay.
And we are pretty close to the deadline for that.

So I don't know whether that's probably too advanced in the process for you guys to be able to pull the trigger, but certainly if you click on the link, you can see a link there for us to sign an NDA.
Yeah.
And I can get that to the client and they approve.
They approve everybody.
I'm assuming they'd be happy to speak to Kevl so we could get a call, set up this week and get through.
I would think, to be honest, it's probably a bit too soon.
Yeah, I don't, I don't think you're going to be able to convince the board to put an offer in within the next month, so.
No, and I mean I, Yeah, I, I think they're going to feel that it's.
Yeah, there's one or two things that have to happen first but interesting.
I mean I think these are, you know, these, these the kinds of things that we're sort of looking for.
So I think, you know, regardless of this situation, maybe you can just keep me in the loop as, as things come up or as you come across things you think might be interesting.
It's, it's more.
Let's call it.
Think of it as kind of media sales that the business is trying to build.
It's got a good technology business, strong ARR.
Good sort of client base.
Which isn't to say, I mean it.
I mean the last acquisition that was made was, Was probably as much technology as it was revenue.
But, but just in terms of just sort of.
Just something to be sor.
Thinking about.
Yeah.
Say if, if, if you come across anything that is sort of kind of, let's call it ad sales orientated.
That would be great to know about.
Yeah, sure.
So I'm going to put you on our mailing list now so you alert for new listings.
Perfect.
So that should come your way.
And yeah, when, when more stuff comes on, you'll get to hear about it.
But certainly if we have something, let me just make sure you're in our CRM as well so we can catch you.
So Kevl is in there, but you're not in there.
So I'll add you in.
Is it Matt?
Yeah, it is, yeah.
Matt Newcomb.
And what's your role?
So I'm MD of this kind of new business we're building.
Okay.
So you're in there as well.
So we will definitely be reaching out to you.
I can see we have done actually with the last few listings around Shopper Media, they just haven't picked up on it.
But yeah, I remember in Skins really well actually I was, I was the founder of a.
Well a music website called gigwise.com but it went on to.
To grow into a network of a bunch of different agencies and I think probably dealt with in Skins all the time.
It was a fantastic technology.
So congratulations on, on building that and thank you.
Well done.
Yeah, only good memories of in Skins we got, we.
We definitely earned a ton of money off that.
Yeah, well, I mean, the CPM.
The CPMs were good, I have to say, you know, back.
Yeah, definitely.
I think they came in at something like 20 odd quid.
I remember it like the first time I started loading up in skins.
Yeah, you do remember it well, Andy, so.
Yeah, that's.
That's exactly right.
So, yeah, no, it was good, it was good.
I mean, we sold at the right time to be fair, but.
But yeah, no, it was good, it was good.
So there's sort of time to have one more swing, I think, at building something that can have an exit.
So we'll see.
Yeah, well.
Well, good luck and it'd be great to work with you.
So I guess if it, if it does boil down to them needing to accelerate, then that's where we would probably come in.
We're able to bring sort of three or four qualified deals every week and so, you know, within a six month period you should be able to, to close something.
So.
Yeah, all good.
All right, well, pleasure meeting you, Matt.
You're a legend.
Living legend.
You too, man.
Enjoy Somerset.
Don't drink too much of the cider, but enjoy the sunshine.
Yeah, I'd like to, yeah.
It's absolutely blazing today.
And yourself, enjoy the rest of your day.
Thanks, mate.
Take care.

summary.overview: The Introduction and Business Development Meeting between Matthew Newcomb, the newly appointed Managing Director at Kevel, and Andy Day from Capital A Group centered on exploring potential collaboration in the realm of retail media acquisition. Matthew shared his background, highlighting his previous experience leading Inskin Media and his focus on acquiring sub-$20M revenue businesses to drive Kevel's inorganic growth strategy. Andy outlined Capital A's dual approach to assisting agency owners with buying and selling businesses, including a specific opportunity with a UK-based shopper media SaaS platform. While acknowledging that it was too early for Kevel to dive into new commitments due to Matthew's recent onboarding, both parties expressed interest in future opportunities, with Andy agreeing to keep Matthew informed on relevant listings and qualified deals to facilitate Kevel's growth ambitions. Action items included adding Matthew to Capital A's mailing list and CRM, as well as Matthew's review of ongoing projects with Kevel's board.

Andy presented Capital A's dual approach in aiding agency owners with buying and selling businesses, specifically mentioning a UK-based SaaS platform in shopper media as a potential opportunity. Although both parties recognized it was too early for Kevel to engage in new commitments due to Matthew's recent onboarding, they expressed mutual interest in future collaborations. Andy committed to keeping Matthew updated on relevant listings and qualified deals. Action items included adding Matthew to Capital A's mailing list and CRM, along with Matthew reviewing ongoing projects with Kevel's board.
